title: Mirabel and the Crown
premise: When the valley's protective wards collapse and the stars vanish, Odile Fairweather learns her guild of ward-keepers was never merely maintaining borders—it was holding a covenant between the human realm and the star-born Fae, and the last signatories are dead. Guided by Mirabel, a fugitive fae noblewoman who has lost her own name to the dark, Odile must cross into the outside world for the first time to gather three shattered keystones before the thirteenth moon turns. Along the way she discovers her guild deliberately erased its members' memories to keep them compliant, and that her own forgotten past binds her to both realms. In the climax, Odile chooses to sacrifice her remaining memories of home to reforge the covenant, restoring the stars but ensuring she can never fully belong anywhere again—until Mirabel gives her a new memory, freely made, as the first act of the renewed pact.
about_author: Marguerite Vane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing folk covenants and boundary charms in rural collections. She writes fantasy about people caught between obligations they never chose.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. On the eve of the guild's annual census, every star above the valley vanishes at once, and the border wards hum then fail. The emotional beat is quiet dread: Odile, always overlooked, notices what no one else will admit—that the elders expected this.

chapters.title: A Guild of Small Duties
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Flashback-laced chapter establishing the Fairweather guild: nine aging members, dwindling magic, rituals maintained by rote. Odile tends the outermost marker stone alone. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as duty.

chapters.title: What Fell from the Dark
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Investigating the broken ward-line, she finds a woman unconscious in the ash-field—Mirabel, half-starved, with no shadow and no name she can speak. Emotional beat: reluctant compassion overriding guild law, which demands strangers be turned away.

chapters.title: The Elders' Silence
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Odile and Elder Bram. The guild convenes; Bram recognizes something in Mirabel and orders her confined. Odile overhears fragments: 'the thirteenth turn,' 'she signed it too.' Emotional beat: betrayal—the protectors knew and said nothing.

chapters.title: Mirabel
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, first time. She wakes caged, remembering only fragments of a court beneath an extinguished sky. She tests Odile during food deliveries and finds a mind that asks questions instead of reciting rules. Emotional beat: two outsiders recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Forgetting
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Searching the guild archive for answers, she finds a ledger listing every member's 'adjustments'—memories ritually removed. Her own page is thick. Emotional beat: horror that her invisibility may have been engineered.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A confession chapter: the covenant required renewal each thirteen-moon cycle; the last signatory died believing someone else would act. Bram removed memories from generations of guild children to keep them from asking why. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into desperation.

chapters.title: Out Past the Markers
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Defying the guild, she frees Mirabel and crosses the fallen ward-line together. Outside, the world is wrong—colorless sky, roads that forget themselves. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of first freedom.

chapters.title: The Road That Forgets
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They reach a village where residents cannot remember yesterday; the starless dark erodes memory first. An old ferryman trades them passage for one true story each. Emotional beat: learning that memory is currency—and Odile has less than she thought.

chapters.title: Keystone: The River Gate
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. First keystone recovered from a drowned shrine, guarded by a river-spirit who demands a memory of water. Odile pays with her memory of learning to swim beside her mother. Emotional beat: grief as the price of progress.

chapters.title: Hunters of the Hollow Court
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Pursuers arrive—fae knights serving whatever consumed the stars, led by Serel, who once loved Mirabel and now cannot remember her. Emotional beat: being hunted by your own forgotten past.

chapters.title: Ash and Covenant
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Ambush on the moor; Mirabel reveals her power by burning the knights' memory-fetters, collapsing afterward. She confesses she was the covenant's fae signatory and fled when the stars began dying. Emotional beat: trust forged in shared failure.

chapters.title: The City Without Names
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They shelter in a city where the dark has taken everyone's names; people wear tokens instead. A token-seller offers Odile a false identity—a belonging without cost. Emotional beat: temptation of comfortable forgetting.

chapters.title: What Odile Paid
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Examining her ledger-page fragment, she realizes her deepest erased memory involves Mirabel—they met once as children across the old ward-line. Emotional beat: vertigo of discovering a friendship older than her knowledge of it.

chapters.title: Serel's Bargain
chapters.summary: Serel's POV. The knight captures Odile and offers her restoration of all stolen memories if she betrays Mirabel. Odile sees her erased childhood whole for one heartbeat. Emotional beat: the cruelest offer—everything back, at the cost of the only person who chose her.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She refuses and escapes using a trick from her erased memories, proving the guild could not truly delete what mattered. Mirabel rescues her; Serel hesitates, something stirring. Emotional beat: selfhood asserted against theft.

chapters.title: Keystone: The Mountain Tooth
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Second keystone won through a climbing trial where each must carry the other's worst memory. Mirabel carries Odile's ledger-grief; Odile carries Mirabel's guilt over abandoning her court. Emotional beat: intimacy built from exchanged burdens.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Moon Rises
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Back in the valley, the guild fractures—some want to flee, some to surrender to the dark. Bram, dying, sends his final memory to Odile by messenger-wisp: instructions for the third keystone and an apology. Emotional beat: too-late honesty.

chapters.title: Keystone: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. They descend into the hollowed fae court where the final keystone sits enthroned amid the devoured stars. Serel blocks the way—but Odile returns his true memory of Mirabel, breaking his servitude. Emotional beat: mercy as weapon.

chapters.title: The Price of Renewal
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The covenant demands a living signatory from each realm, bound by willing sacrifice. Mirabel offers her immortality; the covenant requires more—Odile must give every remaining memory of the valley and guild. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh—survival means losing what you survived for.

chapters.title: Covenant Reforged
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At the moment of signing, stars reignite. Odile stands blank among returning light, unable to remember why she is weeping. Mirabel speaks her name back to her—not the old one, a new one, witnessed and kept. Emotional beat: devastation turning toward grace.

chapters.title: A New Memory, Freely Made
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Odile's POV. Months later: wards restored, guild reformed around consent rather than erasure, Mirabel ambassador between realms. Odile keeps a journal of chosen memories, the first entry written in Mirabel's hand. Emotional beat: belonging rebuilt not as inheritance but as promise.
